dataset_metadata.name: Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime
dataset_metadata.institution: Stanford University / SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
dataset_metadata.citation: Geslin, A., Xu, L., Ganapathi, D. et al. Dynamic cycling enhances battery lifetime. Nat Energy (2024). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-024-01675-8
dataset_metadata.funding: National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship Program (grant no. DGE-1656518); Stanford Chevron Fellowship in Energy

cell_info.cell_notes: Commercial EV energy cells described as silicon oxide-graphite / nickel cobalt aluminium lithium-ion. Cylindrical form factor confirmed by use of four-point contact cylindrical cell fixtures (Maccor Series 4000). Specific cell size (18650/21700) and nominal capacity are not disclosed; all data is normalized by cell nominal capacity. Voltage window 3.1-4.2 V (charge CC-CV C/2 to 4.2 V, 0.05C cutoff). 92 cells tested across 47 protocols over 24 months at 35 degC.

aging_modes.notes: Four discharge protocol types: (1) constant current (with/without rest at 5%, 50%, or 100% SOC), (2) periodic duty cycles with regenerative braking pulses, (3) synthetic profiles derived from real driving field data (highway, urban, combined), (4) real driving profiles from two cities. All cells charged identically: CC-CV C/2 to 4.2 V, 0.05C cutoff. Average discharge C-rates: C/16, C/10, C/5, C/2. Each of the 47 protocols was duplicated; 2 cell failures occurred. EoL defined as 85% SOH based on C/2 RPT discharge capacity.

time_protocol.test_equipment: Maccor Series 4000 battery cycler; CSZ temperature chamber model ZPS-16-2-H/AC
time_protocol.notes: Experiments conducted for over 2 years at SLAC-Stanford Battery Center. Most discharge profiles did not include significant rest periods. Constant current protocols with rest used 6 h rest periods at 5%, 50%, or 100% SOC. Maximum observed EFCs at 85% SOH approximately 1600.

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Raw data contains Time, normalized current (C-rate), Voltage, and normalized capacity. Cycle number, Step, State, Full Step #, and Loop3 fields allow identification of subparts of each cycle. Aging summary files contain charge/discharge capacity and cumulative capacity throughput per cycle. Diagnostic capacities stored in a single multi-index dataframe (diagnostic_capacities.pkl). All capacities are normalized by nominal cell capacity.
rawdata.known_issues: Due to data acquisition limitations, Ohmic resistance was calculated 0.03 s after pulse start (R0.03s). Two cell failures encountered. Four C/16 real driving profiles did not reach lower cutoff voltage and were excluded from analyses but retained in dataset. Highway-based synthetic duty cycles 1a and 1b (C/2 average) and synthetic duty cycle 3 (C/2 average) were excluded due to hardware current limits.

checkup.notes: Diagnostic cycles applied at cycle 0, then after 25, 50, 75, and 100 aging cycles, then every 100 cycles thereafter. Full diagnostic sequence: C/3 reset cycle, voltage-based pulse routine, HPPC routine (separated by another C/3 reset cycle), C/40 RPT, C/2 RPT. RPT voltage range 2.8-4.2 V. Resistances extracted from HPPC at 50% SOC during discharge pulse: R0.03s (Ohmic), R3s (charge-transfer), R10s (polarization). Electrode-specific capacities (Qne, Qpe, QLi) fitted from C/40 RPT using half-cell differential voltage model.

notes: This dataset investigates the effect of dynamic vs. constant current discharge profiles on lithium-ion battery aging under non-accelerated, realistic EV-representative conditions. Key finding: dynamic discharge enhances battery lifetime by up to 38% in EFCs at EoL compared to constant current discharge. Explainable ML (XGBoost + SHAP) identified low-frequency discharge current pulses (~8.2 mHz average) and rest fraction at high SOC as key drivers of degradation differences. The paper was published in Nature Energy, Volume 10, February 2025, pp. 172-180. The article is licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.
